title: Aurum Alpha feature flag evaluation context
description: standards/038-feature-flags.md FF6: what an application sends to a flag provider as targeting context. The provider is a backing service and stores what it receives, so the context is closed to the platform's id vocabulary plus a flat map of declared, non-personal attributes. The id keys $ref the identifiers and observability contracts. The attribute-key denylist and the no-@ rule on string values catch the common spellings of personal data, never the property; whether an attribute would identify a person stays the review question. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

attributeKey.description: FF6: snake_case, and none of the spellings under which personal data usually arrives — email, phone, name (including user_name, full_name, display_name), address, birth dates, ip addresses, national identifiers.

attributeValue.description: FF6: a short scalar. No nested objects (a nested object is how a whole record travels), no arrays, and no string containing @ (which is an email address in almost every case).

targeting_key.description: FF6: the public id the flag's scope names — the user's for a user-scoped flag, the tenant's for a tenant-scoped one. Absent for a global flag. OpenFeature's targetingKey; the feature_flag.context.id on the span; the input to an experiment's assignment (FF10).

tenant_id.description: FF6: the authenticated tenant's public id, established by the authorization layer and copied here; never read from a header a caller controls.

user_id.description: FF6: the user's public id per 020 IP1. Never an internal key, never an email.

environment.description: FF6: which environment is evaluating, spelled as the web client's bootstrap document spells it. Rules keyed on it replace the environment detection 030 SC3 forbids in code.

release_version.description: FF6: the repository's SemVer version (010, Principle 15), for rules that turn on at a release.

service.description: FF6: the service's logical name, for rules scoped to one service in a repository holding several.

attributes.description: FF6: a flat map of declared, non-personal attributes a rule may read — a plan tier, a region code, a device class.
